title: CHARLI3 - Cardano integrated Side-Chain Oracle built on Substrate

ms.promise:
We already have a guiding goal for this project: solving the block limitations using a partner chain. This milestone is all about organizing the team and defining the guiding research questions, scope, and timeline for the project. The ultimate goal of this project is to output a feasibility report, project plan for proof of concept, and public report on our research findings. With those penultimate goals in mind, this milestone begins with defining how we will get to that endpoint. 

For this milestone, the outputs are the following:
・Team member assigned to research
・Preliminary research guiding questions refined and methodology decided upon by team
・Research divided amongst team based on experience and skillset
・Research timeline provided
・Research commences
ms.criteria:
・A project team is assigned
・Guiding research questions provided
・Work assigned to team members and timeline is created
・Research phase begins

ms.report:
Here is a medium article that addresses all of the outputs for this milestone and includes a feasibility report in PDF format.
https://oraclecharli3.medium.com/catalyst-update-oracle-side-chain-5c27eaa3fec9
Reviewer Notes: 
・All questions defined in milestone 1 are immediately addressed in the medium article, but to iterate the answers and focus of the research here they are again (Answers to the outputs required).
・No, see below.
・No, there is no solution that will overcome the block time limitation in the sense that a value can be posted prior to 20 seconds on the chain. Whether an oracle is built on EVM, cosmos, IOG partnerchain, or wherever, this limitation remains.
・Can there be data rate optimizations when building a solution on Substrate and connecting with Cardano via the IOG Partnerchain? Yes. Could there be sub-second data value updates. Yes. Would protocols need to consume these sub-second values via API (or off-chain) then receive verification/validation by oracle nodes 20 seconds later? Yes. 
・Is it feasible to build the Charli3 oracle on Substrate? Yes.
・Are there additional questions requiring the implementation left unanswered until a full implementation is attempted? Yes, that's why you see [WIP] for some answers. Again, these are not requirements for the milestone.
・The research team at Txpipe, after their initial analysis during the feasibility phase, have decided that building on the IOG partnerchain is a feasible option to achieve maximum data rate optimizations. 

Please find within the Feasibility Report ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS (e.g. not part of the guiding questions from the original milestone, nor requiring answers for this milestone). 
The approach the research team took was to literally code/build and test a POC of the oracle solution on Substrate.
